subject: Reserved-node autoscale interruption — post-incident customer update and next steps
participants_external: emma.li@forgeai.com (Emma Li, Head of ML Ops)
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@forgeai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 21:12:00 +0000
Subject: [Redwood] Immediate notice: Reserved-node autoscale interruption impacting ForgeAI jobs

Emma —

Quick update from our side: between 20:48 and 21:02 UTC we observed an autoscaling control-plane error that prevented reserved-node groups from scaling to meet burst demand for your Dedicated pool. As a result, several queued inference requests experienced increased queuing and latencies (~2–6x) for ~14 minutes.

What we immediately did:
- Manually provisioned two additional reserved nodes to your pool and rerouted inflight requests (21:04 UTC).
- Triggered a short-term failover to our compatible hosted model instance for high-priority routes you flagged in the MP endpoint config (21:07 UTC).
- Increased our autoscale controller observability and added temporary stricter rate limits to reduce spike amplification.

We are sorry for the disruption — I know you had critical nightly jobs. We are attaching an initial timeline and cluster metric snapshot so your team can cross-check. We will follow up with a concise root-cause summary and remediation plan within the next 24 hours.

Attachments: cluster-metrics-2026-06-19.png, incident-timeline-20260619.pdf

Can you confirm the names of any jobs that failed or were retried on your side so we can correlate logs? If you'd like, I can set up a 30-minute bridge with our SREs and your SREs in the next hour.

— Rohan

We saw the spike in queue times and multiple nightly inference pipelines (job IDs: forge-nlp-nightly-06019, forge-rank-06019) reported failure/timeout. We failed over some jobs to local fallback infra but that incurred delay and some dropped requests.

— Emma
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@forgeai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 00:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Immediate notice: Reserved-node autoscale interruption impacting ForgeAI jobs

Emma — thanks for the details and for offering the bridge. Our SREs (Hannah) ran a full correlation and I wanted to share the preliminary timeline and proposed next steps. Full postmortem draft attached.

Preliminary timeline (UTC):
- 20:47:11 — spike in pod spin-up requests from your pool reported (concurrent scale events triggered by queued requests).
- 20:48:03 — autoscale controller began rate-limiting due to an unexpected NACK loop between scheduler and controller (controller returned transient 503s to scale requests).
- 21:01:00 — queueing latency exceeded threshold; traffic started to back up.
- 21:04:27 — SRE manual scale commanded and nodes became available at 21:04:27.
- 21:07:40 — failover to hosted-compatible route completed; tail latency normalized by 21:09 UTC.

Root cause (summary):
- A regression in the autoscale controller code path caused a retry storm under specific sequence-length distributions (your traffic pattern triggers this edge case). The controller inadvertently re-enqueued scale requests when it received transient errors from the scheduler, producing a feedback loop.

Immediate mitigations in place:
- Fixed controller backoff logic (hotpatch deployed 20:50 UTC) — stops the feedback loop under retry.
- Added stricter circuit-breaker thresholds on the scheduler-controller path to prevent amplification.
- Added an emergency canary which will run for your pool for 72 hours to ensure stability.

Next steps we propose:
1) Postmortem & patch verification: Hannah to verify the hotpatch telemetry and run a replay against ForgeAI traffic replay dataset.
2) Production hardening: engineer-led follow-up to add longer-term safety (rate limit by tenant, better queueing isolation). Target ETA: 10 business days.
3) Credits: Marcus will coordinate a provisional SLA credit while the postmortem is finalized.
4) Joint call: propose 30-minute call Mon 2026-06-22 16:00 UTC — to review RCA, planned engineering changes, and verify the canary results.

I've attached the postmortem draft and the cluster metric snapshot. If you want the raw controller logs to correlate, say the word and Monica and Hannah will push them to your SRE bucket.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-ForgeAI.docx, cluster-metrics-2026-06-19.png

— Rohan

Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 01:05:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: ForgeAI reserved-node incident — action items and owners

Team — quick internal note to coordinate follow-up after the bridge. Summary in case you missed the first note: autoscale controller regression caused a retry storm and short saturation for ForgeAI's reserved pool; hotpatch and manual nodes mitigated the immediate impact.

Action items (owners):
- Hannah: verify hotpatch telemetry + run 3 replays with ForgeAI traffic dataset (ETA: Mon 06/22 EOD). Push raw controller logs to shared bucket: gs://redwood-incident-logs/forgeai/20260619.
- Monica: confirm log redaction and send log bundle to ForgeAI SRE (ops@forgeai.com) by Mon 06/22 14:00 UTC.
- Marcus: draft provisional credit estimate and coordinate with finance (target: early Mon).
- Rohan: schedule Mon call with ForgeAI, prepare slides with timeline and mitigation plan.

Notes: Engineering follow-up should include tenant-level rate limiting as a high priority. We should also consider adding an automated detection that isolates tenants causing controller pressure to avoid cross-tenant amplification.

Please ack and flag any blockers.

— Rohan
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@forgeai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 18:45:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: remediation completed, proposed credits, and next-steps call

Emma —

Thanks again for the bridge earlier. Quick summary and confirmed actions:

What was done (completed):
- Hotpatch deployed and validated (20:50 UTC). Telemetry shows the controller backoff behaved as expected during replay.
- Emergency canary running on your pool (started 21:10 UTC) — no amplifications observed over the first 20 hours.
- Manual scaling and hosted failover we performed minimized job loss; we correlated 12 failed/retied requests across both nightly jobs you reported.

Provisional credits: Marcus proposes a one-time credit equal to 10% of your June Dedicated invoice while postmortem is finalized. Marcus will confirm with finance and cut a statement of credit by Tue 2026-06-23.

Planned engineering work:
- Tenant-level rate limiting and stronger isolation (ETA: 10 business days).
- Controller backoff codebase hardening and improved test coverage (ETA: 7 business days).

Deliverables we will provide:
1) Final postmortem and RCA (PDF) by Tue 2026-06-23.
2) Raw controller logs and sanitized traces (if you approve) delivered to your SRE bucket.
3) A 30-minute follow-up call Mon 2026-06-22 16:00 UTC to walk the RCA and confirm canary metrics.

Please confirm the call time or propose alternatives. If you accept the log share, Monica will upload the redacted bundle to gs://forgeai-sre-share/ and share credentialed access.

Again, apologies for the disruption. We will follow through on the commitments above.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
